Surah 80: ʿAbasa (He Frowned)

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿He frowned﴾: he scowled, i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿and turned away﴾: he turned aside.

**"That he came to him"**, "Li-an jaa'ahu" (because he came to him). Its position is in the accusative, since it is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose), and its governing element (al-'amil fihi) is "'abasa" (he frowned) or "tawalla" (he turned away), according to the difference between the two schools of thought.

**"The blind man"**: 'Abd Allah ibn Umm Maktum. "Umm Maktum" is his mother, and his father was Shurayh ibn Malik. [It is narrated] that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was calling the nobles of Quraysh to Islam, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me of what Allah has taught you," and he repeated that, not knowing that he (the Prophet) was occupied with the people. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked interrupting his speech, so he frowned and turned away from him. Then this was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to honour him after it, saying: "Welcome to the one for whom my Lord rebuked me." He also appointed him as his deputy over Madinah twice.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verse 3:

﴿And what could make you know?﴾ And what thing makes you aware of the state of this blind man?! ﴿Perhaps he might purify himself﴾: perhaps the blind man would cleanse himself, through what he hears from you, of the filth of ignorance. Its original form is "yatazakka" (يَتَزَكّى), and the ta' was assimilated into the zay (فَأُدْغِمَتِ التاءُ في الزايِ), and likewise:

"Or he might be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him."

(Or he might be reminded): yatta'izu, he takes heed.

(And the reminder would benefit him): nasbuhu ("Asim, other than al-A'sha, read it in the accusative, as a response (jawab) to la'alla; and others read it in the nominative, as a conjunction (atf) upon yadhdhakkaru.

(The reminder): dhikrāka, i.e. your admonition (maw'iẓatuka). That is: you do not know what is expected from him, of purification (tazakki) or of remembrance (tadhakkur). Had you known, that would not have escaped you.

"As for him who considers himself self-sufficient" — that is, whoever was wealthy in terms of property.

﴿As for he who is self-sufficient﴾ — that is, whoever was rich in wealth.

﴿Then you attend to him﴾, you give yourself to him with attention, out of eagerness for his faith. [The word] *tasaddā* (تَصَدّى), with the *tā'* assimilated into the *ṣād* (idghām, the merging of one letter into the next), is the reading of the Hijazi (a reading associated with the people of the Hijaz).
And it is not upon you that he does not purify himself. There is no blame upon you for his not purifying himself through Islam, for upon you is only the conveying (of the message).
﴿But as for he who comes to you eagerly﴾, hastening in pursuit of what is good.
﴿And he fears﴾: [he fears] Allah, or the disbelievers, i.e., their harm in coming to you, or stumbling, as is the habit of the blind.

﴿Fa-anta ʿanhu talahhā﴾ — "you are distracted from him" — tatashaghghalu (you busy yourself with other matters). Its original form is "tatalahhā."

It is related that after this, he never frowned in the face of a poor man, nor did he give attention to a rich man. It is also related that the poor were leaders in the councils of consultation (majlis al-shūrā).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verse 11:

﴿Kalla﴾ (By no means), a rebuke: meaning, do not return to the like of that.

﴿Innaha﴾ (Indeed it), i.e., indeed the surah, or the verses,

﴿tadhkira﴾ (is a reminder), an admonition which must be heeded and acted upon according to what it requires.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verse 12:

﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it.﴾ "Whoever wills" means: whoever Allah wills that he should remember it. Or the pronoun (in ﴿dhakarahu﴾, "remember it") is masculine, because tadhkira (reminder, admonition) has the meaning of dhikr (remembrance) and wa'z (exhortation). The meaning is: whoever wills the remembrance, Allah (Exalted is He) inspires him with it.

﴿In scrolls﴾ is an adjectival qualifier of "a reminder"; that is, it is recorded in scrolls copied from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh). Or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "it is in scrolls,"

﴿honored﴾, with Allah.

﴿exalted﴾, in the sky, or exalted in rank and station,

﴿purified﴾, from being touched by anyone other than the angels, or from what is not the speech of Allah (Exalted).
﴿in the hands of scribes﴾, meaning writers, the plural of "safir" (scribe). That is, the angels copy the books from the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh).

﴿Honourable﴾, upright before God, or noble in regard to sins (i.e., keeping far from them);

﴿obedient﴾, pious ones; plural of "bārr" (one who is dutiful and righteous).

﴿قُتِلَ الإنْسانُ﴾: ﴿Cursed be man.﴾ It means the disbeliever is cursed. Or it refers to Umayya or Utba.

﴿ما أكْفَرَهُ﴾ ﴿How ungrateful he is!﴾ Here "ما أكْفَرَهُ" is an interrogative (istifham) of reproach, meaning: what made him disbelieve? Or it is an exclamation (ta'ajjub), meaning: how intense is his disbelief!

﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾ From what insignificant thing did He create him?! It is an interrogative, and its meaning is affirmation (taqrir), then He explained that thing, saying:

From a drop of seminal fluid He created him and determined him, (i.e., determined him) in whatever form He wills.

Note: The verse quoted is 80:19, and the phrase "فَقَدَّرَهُ" is rendered as "determined him" in line with the commentary's gloss "عَلى ما يَشاءُ مِن خِلْقَةٍ," which is translated as "in whatever form He wills."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verse 20:

﴿Then He made the way easy for him﴾. "Al-sabil" (the way) is in the accusative, governed by an implied "yassara" (made easy), meaning: then He made easy for him the way out of his mother's womb, or He made clear to him the way of good and evil.

Then He caused him to die and assigned him a grave (﴿ثُمَّ أماتَهُ فَأقْبَرَهُ﴾), making him one who has a grave in which he is concealed, not like the beasts, as an honor to him. "Qabara al-mayyit" means he buried the dead person; and "aqbara al-mayyit" means he commanded that he be buried (or he enabled him to bury it) and gave him the means to do so.
{Then when He wills, He will raise him up again}: He will bring him back to life after his death.

﴿Kalla﴾ (lit. "Nay" or "No indeed"), a rebuke to man for disbelief.

﴿Lamma yaqḍi mā amarahu﴾ (﴿Not yet has he fulfilled what He commanded him﴾): this disbeliever has not done what Allah commanded him of faith. When He enumerated the blessings upon him in his own self, from the beginning of his coming into being until he reached [maturity], He followed it with mention of the blessings in what he needs, and so He said:
﴿So let man look at his food﴾: the food that he eats and lives by, how We arranged its provision.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verse 25:

﴿That we﴾, with the vowel fatha, is the reading of Kufan (the reciters of Kufa), in which case it is a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal) for "food"; and with the vowel kasra, on the basis of a resumed sentence (isti'naf), is the reading of the others.

﴿We poured down the water in torrents﴾, meaning the rain, from the clouds.

Then We split the earth with a split.

Qur'anic quotations (usually between ﴿ ﴾) are kept with their markers, and the commentary's remark is rendered as follows:

﴿Then We split the earth with a split﴾, [i.e., by the plants].
﴿So We caused to grow therein grain﴾, such as wheat, barley, and others of what is used for food.

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿وَعِنَبًا﴾ = ﴿and grapes﴾; ﴿وَقَضْبًا﴾ = ﴿and fresh herbage﴾.

Translation:

﴿And grapes﴾: the fruit of the vine, i.e., food and fruit (al-ta'am wa'l-fakiha),

﴿and fresh herbage﴾: rutbah (fresh green fodder). It is named by the verbal noun of "qadaba-hu," meaning he cut it, because it is cut repeatedly, time after time.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 80, verse 30:

﴿And gardens﴾, and orchards,

﴿dense with trees﴾, meaning thick-trunked trees. It is the plural of *ghalbāʾ* (غَلْباءُ).

"And fruit", for you;

"and grass" (abban), pasture for your animals.

﴿مَتاعًا﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning "a benefit" or "an enjoyment."

﴿لَكم ولأنْعامِكُمْ﴾ — "for you and for your cattle."
Then when the Deafening Blast comes, [i.e.] the Blast of the Resurrection, because it deafens the ears, meaning: it makes them deaf. Its response is omitted, because it is evident.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verses 34–35:

﴿On the Day when a man will flee from his brother﴾ ﴿and his mother and his father﴾. (He flees from them) because of the liabilities (tabi'at) between him and them, or because he is preoccupied with himself.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verses 34–35:

﴿On the Day when a man will flee from his brother﴾ ﴿and his mother and his father﴾. (He flees from them) because of the liabilities (tabi'at) between him and them, or because he is preoccupied with himself.

﴿And his companion﴾, his wife,

﴿and his sons﴾. He began with the brother, then the parents, because they are closer to him, then the spouse and the sons, because they are most beloved. It is said: the first to flee from his brother is Habil (Abel); from his parents, Ibrahim (Abraham); from his spouse, Nuh (Noah) and Lut (Lot); and from his son, Nuh (Noah).

For every person among them on that Day there will be a matter that occupies him, in himself.

﴿That occupies him﴾: it suffices him in being concerned with it, and it keeps him preoccupied away from anyone else.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 80, verse 38:

﴿Some faces that Day will be radiant﴾, shining, from standing in prayer at night (qiyam al-layl), or from the traces of ablution (wudu').
ُ﴿Laughing, rejoicing﴾, that is, the owners of these faces, who are the believers, laughing and joyful.
**And faces on that Day will be upon them dust-colored (ghabara)**, ghubār (dust).

﴿Dust will cover them, darkness overspreading them﴾: over the dust there will be a blackness like smoke. And nothing is more dreadful to behold than the gathering of dust-coloured dullness and blackness upon a face.

Those (﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾), the people of this state,

﴿are the disbelievers﴾ (al-kafaratu), in respect of the rights of God,

﴿the wicked﴾ (al-fajaratu), in respect of the rights of people. And since they combined wickedness with disbelief, there was added to the blackness of their faces a dust-like gloom (al-ghabarah).
